talking_points: **Network-adequacy risk:** 22 solo primary-care physicians (age ~66+) in Colorado are actively winding down, and 3 ZIP code(s) already have 2+ winding down at once — including Littleton (80123), La Junta (81050), Colorado Springs (80907) — each a 12-month access-gap risk under Medicare Advantage and state drive-time standards.

**Facility-fee shield:** ~2,489 Medicare patients are attached to these winding-down practices today. If they drift into hospital-owned clinics, the plan pays 2-3x more per identical visit via facility fees. Corner NPs capture those panels at 85-95% of the physician fee schedule — a direct cost-containment shield.

**Auto-assignment targets:** the thinnest-supply counties — Otero County — are where unattributed members and HEDIS gaps will concentrate as these doctors exit. They are prime spots to auto-assign members or co-fund outreach to a new Corner clinic.

**Immediate ask:** fast-track credentialing for Corner in Colorado; 8 practice(s) are the highest priority (winding down with little local backup) and ~69,600 patients sit across all 58 at-risk solo practices statewide.
